success_patterns: When modifying workbooks via script, compute target values in Python and write them as literals unless the task explicitly requires a formula—this avoids fragility from array-formula syntax differences, implicit-intersection behavior, and recalculation engine variations.
When deleting rows, always iterate from the bottom of the sheet upward so row indices do not shift beneath you.
Build lookup dictionaries from source data before modifying target ranges, and normalize keys (strip, case) to handle whitespace variations.
Inspect actual cell values and types with openpyxl before writing solutions, especially for cross-sheet matching and string filtering tasks.
